newsitem.title: USA: Strike at Sun Co Marcus Hook plant possible - Union.
newsitem.headline: Strike at Sun Co Marcus Hook plant possible - Union.

text.p: Union workers could strike at Sun Co's Marcus Hook, Pennsylvania refinery after January 12, according to the president of the local chapter of the the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers International (OCAW) union.

Sun Co and OCAW local 8-109 kicked off negotiations Monday on Sun's plan to trim some 235 workers from the 845 currently employed at the Marcus Hook refinery, which has an estimated crude distillation capicity of 175,000 barrels per day.
"After January 12, we have a 60-day window to cancel the contract and strike," said Bill Lacombe, president of of the local OCAW chapter.
Under the three-year contract signed in early 1996, Sun must give 90 days notice before laying off workers. That formal notification was given December 11.
Lacombe said the union, though aware that job cuts were coming, was taken by surprise by the number of layoffs Sun is seeking.

"Given the staffing levels they're looking at, we're really going to be looking at the safety issues," Lacombe said. The company has previously said the cutbacks would pose no threat to safety at the facility.
Lacombe said that under current contract terms Sun cannot lay off its own workers as long as it employs outside contractors at the facility. Sun has put the number of contractors at about 50.
"I'd be surprised if that's all there are there," Lacombe said. He said most refineries typically use between 150 and 200 contractors.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1626
